item.title: Iran war live: Trump vows to strike Iran ‘hard’ after first clash in month
item.description:
Donald Trump speaks in the Oval Office on Aug. 31, 2026. Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images. For days, Donald Trump’s administration has been on a media blitz to lie to reporters, the public, and the markets about how the president’s illegal war on Iran is going really well, actually. In reality, very few in the U.S. government are buying their own propaganda. “We aren’t winning,” one senior U.S. government official tells Zeteo this week. “Why are you asking me if I think we’re winning? item.title: The Nepal and Tibet flood is a warning: melting snow and ice will bring more disasters around the world | Bill McGuire
item.description:
In Alaska, the Himalayas, the Andes, Greenland, and perhaps also the Alps, deadly chain reactions are just waiting to be triggered You may not have felt it, but the earth beneath our feet is getting twitchier, and global heating is to blame. As temperatures surge and climate breakdown accelerates, interactions between climate and geology are becoming ever more apparent – as marked by last week’s horrific events in Nepal and Tibet . We still have a bit of a blind spot when it comes to the idea that a changing climate can impact what scientists call the geosphere, but the evidence has long been incontestable. In 2021, a similar deluge ripped through a series of mountain valleys in the Indian Himalayan state of Uttarakhand , severely damaging two hydroelectric power plants and taking about 200 lives. item.title: The odds of survival for those trapped after Nepal flood, according to experts
item.description:
Total of 804 confirmed dead and more than 3,000 missing amid threat of fresh inundation ‘Their whole village has disappeared’: frantic hunt for survivors in Kathmandu hospital Rescuers in Nepal and Tibet have battled through leg-sucking mud amid the threat of fresh flooding to search for thousands of people still missing after a deadly wall of water swept through the Himalayan border zone, engulfing entire villages. The latest updates on Sunday put the number of missing at 3,048, including hundreds of foreigners. There was a total of 804 confirmed deaths across Nepal and Tibet, and reports of some bodies swept downstream possibly as far as India. Continue reading...

item.title: Argentinian footballer Lionel Messi announces his retirement
item.description:
The Argentinian’s international career was singular, and his exit is a reminder that all good things come to an end It was among the defining moments of the 2026 World Cup: Lionel Messi standing arms akimbo, looking up towards Argentina’s fervent supporters after losing the final . Tears streamed down his face after his team’s embarrassing loss to Spain in what we now know was Messi’s final match wearing that famous Argentina kit. It was not the first time he’d cried at the tournament. There had been tears of joy in Argentina’s opening match, when Messi rolled back the clock to his glory days with a trio of spectacular goals against Algeria. There had been more when his brace against Austria pushed Argentina through to the knockout round as group winners, and even more when his equalizer against Egypt threw la Albiceleste a much-needed lifeline. item.title: Tariffs spat: Carney bets Canada can defy Trump
item.description:
Meanwhile, Trump posts video of himself kicking over a Lake Ontario sign and replacing it with Lake America sign Donald Trump and Canada continued a verbal duel on Saturday over the US government’s administrative renaming of Lake Ontario, with the Ontario premier erecting a giant sign saying “Lake Ontario. Now and Always” – and the American president posting a video of him tearing down an avatar of that sign, erecting a replacement saying Lake America, and dancing to YMCA. Rhetoric over the naming of Lake Ontario is the public face of an escalating trade dispute between the US and its northern neighbor involving a 50% US tariff on Canadian steel and retaliatory tariffs from Ottawa. item.title: Putin, Xi reaffirm Russia-China ties amid ‘unpredictable’ world
item.description:
Chinese leader Xi Jinping pledged stronger ties with Russia after meeting President Vladimir Putin on Monday, as Beijing flexed its diplomatic might at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan. With 10 member states in attendance, the gathering offers Xi the chance to demonstrate that Beijing has “ friends and options around the world at precisely the moment Washington is alienating many of its allies,” a China adviser in the Biden administration told The New York Times. It’s also a chance for Xi to put a floor under China’s tense relationship with India, which “finds itself a reluctant and defensive participant — unable to move too close to China or identify fully with the anti-Western agenda promoted by Beijing and Moscow,” a Foreign Policy columnist argued. — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: How China buried Tibet flood images after Nepal disaster
item.description:
Rights group claims 300 homes were destroyed in Tibet and number of missing people is ‘far higher’ than Beijing admits A Tibetan advocacy group says hundreds of homes were destroyed on the Tibetan side of the border in last week’s deadly floods, raising questions about Beijing’s official account of the scale of the disaster. Public discussion about the flash floods has been restricted, with security officials in Tibet announcing on Sunday that it had penalised at least 10 people for sharing “false disaster information”. There was no further information on the nature of the penalties. Continue reading...

item.title: Dolly Forever
item.description:
Kristof Ramon, Cor Vos There are no guarantees in sport. A race is never really over until it's over. Nothing lasts forever. Bike racing fans hold these truths to be self evident. Our aphorisms are as fundamental as they are cliché, hardly even worth writing down – but for the last few years, Tadej Pogačar has made us question every one of them and so much more of what we thought we knew about bike racing. Throughout the most dominant stretch in modern cycling history, all but the flattest events on the calendar have seemed like foregone conclusions the moment the UAE Team Emirates-XRG leader decided to take to the start line. And from the moment he put the hammer down in the very first week of this or that race, it really was over for everyone else. At times, this era of inevitability has felt like it might never end. item.title: Data from 911 calls at ICE detention centers must be released under bill going to Gov. Newsom
item.description:
In summary The California Legislature passed a bill that would force disclosure of information about emergency calls at immigrant detention centers. A Democratic lawmaker put it forward after reading news stories in CalMatters. Legislation that would improve public access to information about violence, medical emergencies, and other serious incidents in privately operated detention facilities in California is now heading to the governor’s desk. It would require local agencies to release audio and records of 911 calls and other emergency-service calls originating from the facilities upon request. State Sen.
